matching: Items 1-2 gap-fill naming an object from its use; 3-4 choice of object in context; EC = wrong classroom noun for its use (I [verb] ... with my X); FP = one sentence naming an object on your desk/in your bag; transfer = a teacher's list instruction. All nouns EVP A1, prompts 8-14 words. Item order identical across forms: 1-2 controlled gap-fill, 3-4 controlled choice, 5-6 error correction, 7-8 free production (target_form_0_1_2), 9 transfer. Review round 1: slots 5-6 are now wrong-object errors (wrong classroom noun for its use), not article omission. Re-review round 2: B-6 and C-6 replaced (notebook/pencil case and close the board were not certain errors); all six EC items now follow one pattern; l1ErrorTypes in outcomes.json cleared because lexical object confusion has no schema enum value. Review round 3: slots 5-6 rewritten as realistic Arabic-L1 spelling slips on a classroom noun (slot 5 = phon_p_b, p written as b: bencil/ben/baper; slot 6 = spelling_vowel, vowel omitted: calculter/dictionry/notbook); the earlier wrong-object swaps were not real learner errors. The corrected noun is not shown elsewhere in the same form. l1ErrorTypes in outcomes.json set to phon_p_b, spelling_vowel. Review round 4: phon_p_b is an audio-only type in docs/LEARNING_OUTCOMES.md, so the typed slot-5 slips (bencil/ben/baper) are now tagged spelling_vowel, the only typed-spelling enum value; outcomes.json l1ErrorTypes = [spelling_vowel]. A consonant-spelling enum value is a user decision. C-6 now also accepts 'in a notebook', like the other slot 5-6 items. User decisions (A1-A2): vocabulary validity - each form keeps one spelling error-correction item (slot 5); slot 6 is now a meaning error (Arabic-L1 polysemy or calque on an A1 word), with exactly one correct fix and the answer word not shown elsewhere in the form.
